visual: Chinese dining table; Mei pours tea for auntie
vo: In China, many people would use a kinship word instead — like 'auntie' — even if she's not a relative.

visual: Close-up Mei; small relationship map appears
vo: It's not about being formal. It's about marking the relationship.

visual: US birthday party; Alex tears wrapping paper
vo: In the US, you open a gift right away. It shows you're excited.

visual: Chinese home; Mei receives gift with both hands, thanks, sets it aside
vo: In many Chinese homes, it can feel more polite to thank the person first — and open it later.

visual: US restaurant bill; card reader shows 20% tip
vo: In the US, leaving a tip is expected.

visual: Chinese noodle shop; Mei scans QR code, exact amount; owner waves off tip
vo: In China, most restaurants don't expect one. The menu price is usually the price.
